item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
So, the entire time I was reading this, I was thinking, "Oh, Blackwood's probably not the same as the slug they have under containment," or, "oh, Charlie must not realize how bizarre his uncle is."

But the last line…

Sticks and stones may break my bones
but words can sucker punch me.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
If you ask me, I think everyone in the Foundation-verse is a slug. Foundation personnel, SCPs, Groups of Interest, everyone and everything.

The only reason the Foundation is containing Lord Blackwood, George Phillip Harris the Fourth, and Charlie Blackwood and labeling them alone as slugs is as a form of Freudian displacement to cope with their own existence as slugs.

Just give them some time and they'll eventually confront the truth on their own.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I had the uncle pegged as Blackwood fairly early on based on 'Teddy', then began to doubt it when you described the uncle. The ending works well, though. Wondering how you see the slug deal working, as in the original article Blackwood is stored in a small aquarium tank and survives on slug feed, so presumably it's not simply that other people perceive him and his relatives as slugs.

One slight inconsistency:
"Uncle Teddy doesn't look a day over seventy or so, and he hasn't changed in all the years I've known him"
"I suppose I have been forty-nine for quite awhile now."

Wasn't sure if we were meant to chalk this up to the protagonist's perception of Teddy from the perspective of a child, Blackwood being nonsensical, or what.
